Culture

Festivals, Sarna and the akhra — where the language lives

Mundari is not only spoken, it is also sung and danced. 𞓛𞓟𞓛𞓟𞓨 Susun means song, 𞓡𞓟𞓣𞓕𞓔 duraŋ means dance, and the 𞓕𞓢𞓞𞓣𞓕 akhra in the middle of the village is the open ground where the whole village gathers on festival nights.

Sarna and Singbonga

The traditional religion of the Munda community is Sarna — its centre is the sacred grove of trees near the village (the sarna / jaher), not a temple building. The village priest, the 𞓑𞓕𞓞𞓕𞓨 Pahan, worships the village deities (𞓞𞓕𞓝𞓟 𞓗𞓐𞓔𞓦𞓕𞓢𞓐 Hatu Boŋgako) and the spirits of the ancestors. The supreme deity is 𞓛𞓚𞓔𞓗𞓐𞓔𞓦𞓕 Singbonga — the Sun god.

A translation warning: 𞓗𞓐𞓔𞓦𞓕 boŋga means deity / spirit / power — do not simply replace it with the monotheistic word “God”, and never call a Sarna grove a “temple”.

𞓛𞓕𞓣𞓞𞓟𞓒Sarhul / Baha Parab

March–April · the festival of flowers

New sal flowers are offered at the Sarna grove; the new year and spring are welcomed.

Open the full Sarhul page →

𞓢𞓕𞓣𞓕𞓧Karam

August–September

Unmarried young people bring a Karam branch and sing and dance all night, wishing prosperity for the village.

Open the full Karam page →

𞓧𞓕𞓦𞓤Mage Parab

Paush full moon · January–February

A festival of remembering and honouring the ancestors.

Open the full Mage Parab page →

𞓛𞓐𞓞𞓣𞓕𞓚Sohrai

October–November

Lamps are lit, the cattle shed is washed and decorated, and rice-beer (𞓚𞓒𞓚 ili) is sprinkled.

Open the full Sohrai page →

𞓑𞓞𞓕𞓦𞓟Phagu

February–March

A festival of communal hunting and colours — its time falls around Holi.

Open the full Phagu page →

Remembering the Ulgulan

1899–1900 · Birsa Munda

Birsa Munda's great uprising (the Ulgulan) still lives on in the language and its songs; it was because of it that the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 was made. The Mundari place-name endings — -𞓞𞓕𞓝𞓟, -𞓗𞓤𞓣𞓕, -𞓦𞓟𞓝𞓟, -𞓐𞓣𞓕 -hatu, -bera, -gutu, -ora — still mark the old Mundari land on the maps of Jharkhand today.

Mundari Samaj

Our Language. Our Identity. Our Heritage. Mundari Samaj is a digital platform dedicated to preserving, documenting, promoting and sharing the Mundari language and the histories, cultures, traditions and knowledge of Munda communities.
